title: Chelsea Emergency Help Points
summary: 24-hour A&E hospitals, urgent care clinics, flood risks, and essential supplies for Chelsea.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, call 999 or 112 immediately.

1. Nearest 24-Hour A&E Hospitals:
- Chelsea and Westminster Hospital: 369 Fulham Road, SW10 9NH. From South Kensington station: ~15 min walk southwest along Pelham Street and Fulham Road (~0.7 miles), or take bus 14 or 414 southwest along Fulham Road (~8 mins). From Sloane Square station: ~22 min walk west along King's Road and Sydney Street (~1.1 miles), or take bus 11 or 211 west towards Fulham (~12 mins). From Imperial Wharf station: ~18 min walk northeast along Harwood Road and Fulham Road (~0.9 miles).
- St Thomas' Hospital: Westminster Bridge Road, SE1 7EH. From Sloane Square station: ~45 min walk east along Pimlico Road and Millbank, or take bus 11 or 211 east towards Westminster (~25 mins).
- St Mary's Hospital (Major Trauma Centre): Praed Street, Paddington, W2 1NY. From South Kensington station: ~35 min walk north via Exhibition Road and Hyde Park, or take bus 14 / 27 north towards Paddington (~25 mins).

2. NHS Urgent Treatment Centres (UTC):
- Chelsea and Westminster Urgent Treatment Centre: 369 Fulham Road, SW10 9NH (co-located at the hospital's A&E entrance; accessible via bus 14, 211, or 414).

3. Local Hazards & Flood Risks:
- The River Thames forms the southern boundary along Chelsea Embankment, Cheyne Walk, and Lots Road; high tidal surge events and surface drainage back-up present flood hazards along waterfront streets and underground basements.

4. Supplies & Essentials:
Pharmacies and major supermarket chains along King's Road, Fulham Road, Sloane Square, and Duke of York Square supply bottled drinking water, sanitary products, and critical prescription pharmaceuticals.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
